rules.title: Xcode DerivedData
rules.detail: Intermediate build products of your projects. The next build of each project will take longer.

rules.title: Device support symbols (DeviceSupport)
rules.detail: Xcode downloads these from an iPhone/iPad when you connect it. After deletion, the first connection of a device will take longer.

rules.title: Xcode and simulator caches
rules.detail: Internal Xcode and CoreSimulator caches. They are rebuilt on the next launch.

rules.title: Xcode Archives
rules.detail: Build archives together with their dSYMs. Without them you cannot symbolicate crashes of versions you have already released.

rules.title: iOS simulator runtimes
rules.detail: iOS/watchOS images for simulators, 7–10 GB each. Removed with `xcrun simctl runtime delete`. You can download the runtime you need again in Xcode settings (Components). Duplicates (17.0 and 17.0.1) are marked.

rules.title: Simulators (devices)
rules.detail: Created simulators together with the data of the apps installed on them. Removed with `xcrun simctl delete`. New ones are created in Xcode → Window → Devices and Simulators.

rules.title: Gradle caches
rules.detail: Downloaded dependencies and build results. The next Android project build will download everything again (internet required).

rules.title: Gradle distributions (wrapper)
rules.detail: Separate Gradle versions for projects. Gradle downloads the version it needs on the next build.

rules.title: JDKs downloaded by Gradle
rules.detail: Toolchain JDKs that Gradle downloaded by itself. They are downloaded again when needed.

rules.title: Android emulators (AVD)
rules.detail: Virtual device images with all their data (usually 5–15 GB each). Create them again in Android Studio → Device Manager.

rules.title: Android NDK versions
rules.detail: Individual NDK versions. Gradle downloads the one you need if the project specifies it (ndkVersion).

rules.title: npm cache
rules.detail: Cache of downloaded packages. npm downloads what it needs on the next install.

rules.title: Yarn cache
rules.detail: Yarn package cache. Downloaded again on the next install.

rules.title: CocoaPods cache
rules.detail: Cache of downloaded pods. `pod install` downloads what it needs.

rules.title: Swift Package Manager cache
rules.detail: Package clones and artifacts. Xcode downloads them again when it resolves dependencies.

rules.title: Homebrew cache
rules.detail: Downloaded installers and indexes. For old versions of formulae there is a separate `brew cleanup`.

rules.title: Build tool caches (node-gyp, Next.js, TypeScript, pip)
rules.detail: Caches of build tools. They are recreated on next use.

rules.title: Playwright browsers
rules.detail: Chromium/Firefox/WebKit downloaded for tests. Restore them with `npx playwright install`.

rules.title: Caches of old Android Studio versions
rules.detail: Indexes and caches of versions you have not used for a long time. The latest version and anything changed within 30 days are kept.

rules.title: Caches of old JetBrains IDE versions
rules.detail: Indexes and caches of old versions of WebStorm, IntelliJ, etc. The latest version and anything changed within 30 days are kept.

rules.title: Settings of old Android Studio versions
rules.detail: Settings, plugins and local history of versions you have not used for a long time (30+ days). Careful: this is not a cache.

rules.title: Settings of old JetBrains IDE versions
rules.detail: Settings and plugins of old versions (unchanged for 30+ days). Careful: this is not a cache.

rules.title: Adobe: video cache (Media Cache, Peak Files)
rules.detail: Cache of Premiere Pro, After Effects, Media Encoder. Often takes tens of GB. It rebuilds itself, but the first preview of your projects will be slower.

rules.title: Adobe: app caches
rules.detail: Caches of Photoshop, Illustrator, Lightroom, Camera Raw, After Effects (disk cache) and others. They are rebuilt, but the first launch may take longer.

rules.title: Caches of Figma, Discord, Slack and other apps
rules.detail: Web caches of Electron/Chromium apps (Figma, Discord, Slack, Notion, VS Code…). Profiles, passwords and documents are never touched, only the Cache folders. The apps rebuild them themselves.

rules.title: Sandboxed app caches in Containers (Affinity, Pixelmator…)
rules.detail: Caches of apps that run in a sandbox. Apple's system apps are not listed here. They are rebuilt automatically.

rules.title: Caches in Group Containers
rules.detail: Shared caches of apps from the same developer. System (Apple) ones are not listed here.

rules.title: Safari cache
rules.detail: Page cache only. Bookmarks, history and passwords are kept. Pages will load slower at first. Requires Full Disk Access.

rules.title: Telegram: downloaded media (cache)
rules.detail: Photos, videos and files from chats that Telegram saved on disk. Usually several GB. They are downloaded again from the cloud. Secret chats and files that have not been sent yet cannot be restored. Telegram must be closed.

rules.title: Chrome cache
rules.detail: Page cache only. Your profile, bookmarks and passwords are never touched. Pages will load slower at first.

rules.title: Claude: virtual machine image
rules.detail: The VM image that Claude for desktop creates for isolated tasks. It is created again when needed.

rules.title: Caches of other apps
rules.detail: Caches of apps not covered by other rules. System (com.apple.*) and running apps are skipped.

rules.title: App logs
rules.detail: Logs and crash reports. Nobody needs them unless you are investigating a problem.

rules.title: System caches (/Library/Caches)
rules.detail: Caches shared by all users. macOS will ask for the administrator password. Off by default.

rules.title: System logs (/Library/Logs)
rules.detail: Logs shared by all users. macOS will ask for the administrator password. Off by default.

rules.title: Apple system service caches (Containers)
rules.detail: Caches of macOS services, for example photo analysis (mediaanalysisd) and connecting devices to Xcode. They take gigabytes. macOS rebuilds them, but background photo indexing may load your Mac for a while. Off by default.

rules.title: Mail attachments downloaded to disk
rules.detail: Copies of attachments that Mail saved for viewing. For IMAP mail the originals stay on the server, but for POP they may be the only copy. Requires Full Disk Access.

rules.title: iPhone/iPad update files (.ipsw)
rules.detail: Firmware that Finder downloaded when updating a device. It is downloaded again if needed.

rules.title: Trash
rules.detail: Permanently deletes everything in the Trash. Requires Full Disk Access. You cannot undo this.
